input.quote: (e) THE EXPRESS WARRANTIES IN THIS AGREEMENT SHALL BE IN LIEU OF ALL OTHER WARRANTIES, EXPRESS OR IMPLIED, INCLUDING THE IMPLIED WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY, FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE.
input.rationale: Section 5 gives only compliance-with-law (5(a)), authority/rights (5(b)), non-infringement (5(c)) and anti-bribery (5(d)) warranties. There is no express warranty that the Services or Works will conform to the Specifications or documentation, no warranty period, no no-malicious-code warranty, and no repair/replace/refund remedy. The workmanlike standard in Paragraph 1(b) is a bare performance covenant with no stated remedy, and Section 4's "ACCEPTANCE" heading has no acceptance mechanics to fall back on. Because 5(e) puts the express warranties "in lieu of all other warranties, express or implied," the implied warranties of merchantability and fitness are disclaimed while nothing conformance-related replaces them, leaving Clear Capital close to the walk-away "AS IS" position. The redline inserts a conformance warranty (12 months for software deliverables, 90 days for Services), a no-malicious-code warranty, and an at-Contractor's-option re-perform/repair/replace-or-refund remedy, and confirms the disclaimer does not swallow the express warranties; the 90/30-day fallback remains available.

proposal.summary: Add express performance/conformance warranty with repair-replace-refund remedy and carve it out of the disclaimer
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 5 contains rights and compliance reps but no warranty that the Services and Works will actually conform to the Specifications, and no remedy if they do not, so we have added a conformance warranty (12 months for software deliverables, 90 days for Services), a no-malicious-code warranty, and a re-perform/repair/refund remedy, and confirmed the disclaimer in 5(e) does not cut it back. Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

Rule:
ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.
Severity: low
Category: insurance
Position — preferred:
Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

Position — fallback:
E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.
Position — walk-away:
No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.
Detection guidance:
Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.
Model language:
Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.

content.text:
**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

The agreement contains no audit, inspection, or verification right running against us. I confirmed this by:

- **Term searches**: "audit", "inspect", "verif" returned zero hits; "records" hits relate only to IP ownership (§ 4(b)(i)–(ii)) and the definition of Confidential Information (§ 7); "access" hits only § 1, which runs *in our favor* (Contractor must comply with Company's computer-system security policies).
- **Full read of the two candidate sections**: § 3 (Compensation) imposes billing/supporting-detail obligations on the Contractor, not verification rights over us. § 4 (Ownership/Acceptance) contains no examination or entry rights.

Because payment flows one way — RadialSpark invoices Clear Capital with time-and-materials detail — there is no usage metric or underpayment exposure for a vendor audit to police. The absence of any audit right is better for us than the preferred position (annual, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, vendor cost, no system access), so the smallest correct edit is none. Adding audit machinery here would only create a right that does not currently exist.

One adjacent observation, outside this rule's scope and not flagged: § 3(b) lets the Contractor "change rates with 30 days notice to Company" unilaterally, and § 3(a) reimburses out-of-pocket expenses. If the deal team wants assurance on time-and-materials billing accuracy, the appropriate move is a *customer-side* audit right over Contractor's records — the mirror image of this rule — which would need to be raised under a separate pricing or records-retention playbook item.

content.text:
**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

The agreement imposes no take-or-pay exposure on Clear Capital:

- **§ 3(a) (p0013)** — Compensation is time-and-materials, "as set forth in each Statement of Work." Fees track work actually performed, with no floor.
- **§ 1(a) (p0004)** — Contractor is retained "on a task by task basis," confirming purchases arise only as SOWs are agreed, not from a standing volume obligation.
- **§ 6(b) (p0033)** — On termination, Contractor is paid only "fees and expenses that have been incurred or earned ... through the effective date." That is a true-up, not a shortfall penalty, and there is no early-termination or cancellation fee.

A regex sweep for *minimum, shortfall, take-or-pay, retainer, guarantee, commit, exclusiv, volume, non-refundable* surfaced only unrelated hits (IP ownership in § 4, entire-agreement in § 7).

Two points worth noting for the file, neither of which triggers this rule:

1. **§ 6(a)** permits convenience termination only when no SOW is outstanding. That constrains our exit path, but it compels no minimum quantity — better handled under the term/termination rule.
2. **Residual SOW risk.** Minimums could be smuggled into an individual Statement of Work, which we haven't seen. § 1(a)'s provision that this Agreement controls over conflicting SOW terms mitigates but does not fully foreclose this, since a minimum in an SOW arguably supplements rather than conflicts with silence here. Worth a look when SOWs are papered.

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
The Agreement contains no minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay, shortfall or volume restriction binding Clear Capital. Section 3(a) compensates Contractor on a time-and-materials basis solely as set forth in each Statement of Work, and Section 1(a) engages Contractor "on a task by task basis," so fees are payable only for services actually ordered and performed — our preferred position. A targeted regex search for "minimum", "shortfall", "take-or-pay", "retainer", "guarantee", "commit", "volume" and "non-refundable" returned only unrelated hits (exclusive-property and entire-agreement language in Sections 4 and 7). Section 6(b) caps amounts on termination at "all fees and expenses that have been incurred or earned ... through the effective date of such termination," which is a true-up rather than a penalty, and no early-termination or cancellation fee appears. Section 6(a)'s limit on convenience termination while an SOW is outstanding is a term/exit-right issue rather than a purchase commitment, and it creates no obligation to buy a minimum quantity. Residual risk sits in individual Statements of Work, which are not before us; helpfully, Section 1(a) provides that this Agreement controls over conflicting SOW provisions. No redline required.

content.text:
**Finding: Deviation (medium) — no express performance/conformance warranty or remedy.**

What I found:
- **§5 warranties are all "rights and compliance" type only**: 5(a) compliance with law (and only "to its knowledge"), 5(b) authority/rights, 5(c) non-infringement, 5(d) anti-bribery. Nothing warrants that the Services or Works will actually work or conform to the Specifications.
- **No warranty period and no remedy** anywhere — no repair, replacement, re-performance or refund.
- **§1(b)** has a workmanlike-manner covenant, but it is a bare performance obligation with no warranty framing or remedy attached.
- **§4 is titled "ACCEPTANCE"** but contains no acceptance or rejection mechanics, so there is no alternative route to a conformance remedy.
- **§5(e) disclaims implied warranties** ("in lieu of all other warranties, express or implied") — it does not swallow express warranties, but with no conformance warranty present the net effect approaches the walk-away "AS IS" position.

Redline (validated, `ok:true`) inserts a new §5(f): conformance warranty of 12 months for software deliverables / 90 days for Services, a no-malicious-code warranty, an at-Contractor's-option re-perform/repair/replace remedy with refund if not cured in 30 days, and an express confirmation that 5(e) does not cut back the express warranties. Fallback of 90/30 days offered in the comment.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.


Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Section 5 gives only compliance-with-law (5(a)), authority/rights (5(b)), non-infringement (5(c)) and anti-bribery (5(d)) warranties. There is no express warranty that the Services or Works will conform to the Specifications or documentation, no warranty period, no no-malicious-code warranty, and no repair/replace/refund remedy. The workmanlike standard in Paragraph 1(b) is a bare performance covenant with no stated remedy, and Section 4's "ACCEPTANCE" heading has no acceptance mechanics to fall back on. Because 5(e) puts the express warranties "in lieu of all other warranties, express or implied," the implied warranties of merchantability and fitness are disclaimed while nothing conformance-related replaces them, leaving Clear Capital close to the walk-away "AS IS" position. The redline inserts a conformance warranty (12 months for software deliverables, 90 days for Services), a no-malicious-code warranty, and an at-Contractor's-option re-perform/repair/replace-or-refund remedy, and confirms the disclaimer does not swallow the express warranties; the 90/30-day fallback remains available.

input.comment: [Playbook] Section 6 covers notice and final fees but says nothing about exit: we have no right to wind-down help and no assurance our data and Confidential Information come back or are deleted. We have added a new Section 6(c) giving us up to six months of transition assistance at Contractor's then-current rates, return of our data in a machine-readable format within thirty days, and certified deletion thereafter. If six months is an issue, we can accept ninety days of assistance provided the thirty-day export and deletion certificate remain.

Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.

Rule:
ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.
Severity: low
Category: insurance
Position — preferred:
Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

Position — fallback:
E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.
Position — walk-away:
No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.
Detection guidance:
Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.
Model language:
Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

The agreement contains no audit, inspection, or verification right running against us. I confirmed this by:

- **Term searches**: "audit", "inspect", "verif" returned zero hits; "records" hits relate only to IP ownership (§ 4(b)(i)–(ii)) and the definition of Confidential Information (§ 7); "access" hits only § 1, which runs *in our favor* (Contractor must comply with Company's computer-system security policies).

Because payment flows one way — RadialSpark invoices Clear Capital with time-and-materials detail — there is no usage metric or underpayment exposure for a vendor audit to police. The absence of any audit right is better for us than the preferred position (annual, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, vendor cost, no system access), so the smallest correct edit is none. If the deal team wants assurance on time-and-materials billing accuracy, the appropriate move is a *customer-side* audit right over Contractor's records — the mirror image of this rule — which would need to be raised under a separate pricing or records-retention playbook item.

input.quote: Upon any such termination, Contractor will be paid all fees and expenses that have been incurred or earned in connection with the performance of the Services through the effective date of such termination.
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no liquidated damages, penalty, late-payment charge, minimum-commitment or early-termination fee payable by Clear Capital. Compensation (§ 3) is strictly time-and-materials plus actual out-of-pocket expenses, and both termination provisions (§ 6(b) and the mis-numbered § 7(c)) limit Company's post-termination payment obligation to fees and expenses actually incurred or earned through the effective date of termination — an accrued-amounts formulation, not a liquidated sum. Section 7 addresses only liability caps, consequential damages waiver and attorneys' fees; it imposes no stipulated damages on Company (and § 5 even relieves Company of any fee obligation on certain terminations). Nothing to flag; the preferred position (no Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties) is already met, so no redline is proposed.

input.rationale: Section 6 (Termination) addresses only termination notice, payment of Contractor's accrued fees, and assignment of Works in progress. It contains no post-termination transition assistance, no obligation to return Company data or Confidential Information, and no deletion/certification requirement. Section 4 (Ownership) establishes that Works are Company property and Section 8 restricts use of Confidential Information, but neither creates any return, export or destruction obligation on exit — a targeted search for "return", "transition", "export", "delete", "destroy" and "migrat" returned no results anywhere in the agreement. On a services/development engagement where Contractor holds Company records, data and Works, this absence is a deviation warranting insertion. The proposed new Section 6(c) tracks the preferred position (six months of assistance at Contractor's then-current rates, return within thirty days in machine-readable format, certified deletion thereafter) and uses the agreement's existing defined terms ("Works", "Confidential Information") for consistency. Fallback of ninety days' assistance is offered in the comment.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

input.quote: (b) In addition, either party may terminate this Agreement or any outstanding Statement of Work, upon fifteen (15) days written notice to the other party, in the event such other party breaches a material term of this Agreement or any Statement of Work and such breach remains uncured at the end of such fifteen (15) day period. input.rationale: Section 6 (Termination) addresses only termination notice, payment of Contractor's accrued fees, and assignment of Works in progress. It contains no post-termination transition assistance, no obligation to return Company data or Confidential Information, and no deletion/certification requirement. Section 4 (Ownership) establishes that Works are Company property and Section 8 restricts use of Confidential Information, but neither creates any return, export or destruction obligation on exit — a targeted search for "return", "transition", "export", "delete", "destroy" and "migrat" returned no results anywhere in the agreement. On a services/development engagement where Contractor holds Company records, data and Works, this absence is a deviation warranting insertion. The proposed new Section 6(c) tracks the preferred position (six months of assistance at Contractor's then-current rates, return within thirty days in machine-readable format, certified deletion thereafter) and uses the agreement's existing defined terms ("Works", "Confidential Information") for consistency. Fallback of ninety days' assistance is offered in the comment.

proposal.summary: Insert transition assistance, data return and certified deletion obligations in Section 6 (Termination).
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 6 covers notice and final fees but says nothing about exit: we have no right to wind-down help and no assurance our data and Confidential Information come back or are deleted. We have added a new Section 6(c) giving us up to six months of transition assistance at Contractor's then-current rates, return of our data in a machine-readable format within thirty days, and certified deletion thereafter. If six months is an issue, we can accept ninety days of assistance provided the thirty-day export and deletion certificate remain.

ops.text: (c) Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement or any Statement of Work for any reason, Contractor shall (i) at Company's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Contractor's then-current rates; (ii) within thirty (30) days of such expiry or termination, return to Company all Works, Confidential Information and other Company data and materials then in Contractor's possession or control, in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (iii) thereafter delete all such Confidential Information, data and materials from its systems and certify such deletion to Company in writing.

input.quote: 14. INSURANCE. Throughout the term of this Agreement, Contractor shall maintain workers compensation insurance in the amount required by statute, comprehensive general liability insurance with coverage of at least one million dollars ($1,000,000) and professional errors and omissions insurance for bodily injury, property damage or other losses with coverage of at least one million dollars ($1,000,000), in connection with the provision of Services by Contractor pursuant to the terms of this Agreement.
input.rationale: An insurance clause is present at Section 14 (p0048), so this is a partial-coverage deviation rather than a missing clause. It already satisfies two elements of the preferred position — workers' compensation as required by statute, and certificates of insurance on request with notice of material change. Three gaps remain: (i) CGL states only a $1,000,000 limit with no $2,000,000 aggregate; (ii) professional E&O is $1,000,000 against our preferred $2,000,000; and (iii) there is no cyber/privacy liability coverage at all. Cyber coverage is squarely warranted here: Section 1(c) (p0007) contemplates Contractor personnel working at Company facilities and accessing Company computer systems, and Section 8 (p0038) confirms Contractor obtains Company data, records and Confidential Information in performing the Services. A vendor with premises access and access to our data and systems with no cyber coverage sits at the playbook walk-away line. The document defines no "Customer Data" term, so the redline ties the cyber trigger to Company data and Confidential Information as defined in Section 8. We also added the one-year post-term tail and "at its own expense" from the model language, since E&O and cyber claims are typically made after the engagement ends. The edit is a single in-place amendment to the existing limits sentence, leaving the workers' compensation, certificate and notice provisions untouched. We did not challenge the "or self-insurance" language, which is a lower-value point at this severity. Fallback of E&O $1M (already met) plus cyber $2M is offered in the comment, since the cyber limit is the element we most need.

proposal.summary: Bring Contractor's insurance limits up to playbook levels: CGL 1M/2M aggregate, E&O 2M, add cyber liability 5M, and extend coverage one year post-term.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Contractor personnel may work at our facilities and access our systems and Confidential Information, so we have aligned the limits with our standard position: general liability of USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate, E&O of USD 2M, and cyber liability of USD 5M, maintained through the term and for one year after. If USD 5M cyber is not available on Contractor's program, we can accept E&O of USD 1M and cyber of USD 2M as a fallback.

Rule:
ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.
Severity: low
Category: insurance
Position — preferred:
Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

Position — fallback:
E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.
Position — walk-away:
No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.
Detection guidance:
Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.
Model language:
Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

input.quote: 14. INSURANCE. Throughout the term of this Agreement, Contractor shall maintain workers compensation insurance in the amount required by statute, comprehensive general liability insurance with coverage of at least one million dollars ($1,000,000) and professional errors and omissions insurance for bodily injury, property damage or other losses with coverage of at least one million dollars ($1,000,000), in connection with the provision of Services by Contractor pursuant to the terms of this Agreement.
input.rationale: An insurance clause is present at Section 14 (p0048), so this is a partial-coverage deviation rather than a missing clause. It already satisfies two elements of the preferred position — workers' compensation as required by statute, and certificates of insurance on request with notice of material change. Three gaps remain: (i) CGL states only a $1,000,000 limit with no $2,000,000 aggregate; (ii) professional E&O is $1,000,000 against our preferred $2,000,000; and (iii) there is no cyber/privacy liability coverage at all. Cyber coverage is squarely warranted here: Section 1(c) (p0007) contemplates Contractor personnel working at Company facilities and accessing Company computer systems, and Section 8 (p0038) confirms Contractor obtains Company data, records and Confidential Information in performing the Services. A vendor with premises access and access to our data and systems with no cyber coverage sits at the playbook walk-away line. The document defines no "Customer Data" term, so the redline ties the cyber trigger to Company data and Confidential Information as defined in Section 8. We also added the one-year post-term tail and "at its own expense" from the model language, since E&O and cyber claims are typically made after the engagement ends. The edit is a single in-place amendment to the existing limits sentence, leaving the workers' compensation, certificate and notice provisions untouched. We did not challenge the "or self-insurance" language, which is a lower-value point at this severity. Fallback of E&O $1M (already met) plus cyber $2M is offered in the comment, since the cyber limit is the element we most need.

proposal.summary: Bring Contractor's insurance limits up to playbook levels: CGL 1M/2M aggregate, E&O 2M, add cyber liability 5M, and extend coverage one year post-term.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Contractor personnel may work at our facilities and access our systems and Confidential Information, so we have aligned the limits with our standard position: general liability of USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate, E&O of USD 2M, and cyber liability of USD 5M, maintained through the term and for one year after. If USD 5M cyber is not available on Contractor's program, we can accept E&O of USD 1M and cyber of USD 2M as a fallback.

The repair was to the finding's rationale, not the document. The verifier's own analysis confirmed the substance was right, so the only defect worth curing was that my rationale did not pre-empt the failed deterministic check. The resubmitted finding now:

Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
Compliant by absence. Searches for "audit", "inspect", "verif", "records" and "access", plus full reads of § 3 (Compensation) and § 4 (Ownership/Acceptance), confirm the Agreement grants RadialSpark no audit, inspection or verification right over Clear Capital's records, usage or systems, and no right of access to our systems. Obligations run the other way: under § 3(b) the Contractor must invoice with supporting detail, dates and hours, so substantiation flows from Contractor to Company. The only access-related provision (§ 1, p0007) also runs in our favor, requiring Contractor to comply with Company's computer-system access and security policies. Because payment is time-and-materials billed by the Contractor, there is no usage metric or underpayment exposure for a vendor audit to police. The failed deterministic check for "audit frequency limited" is an artifact of compliance-by-absence: there is no audit clause to which frequency, notice or cost limits could attach, so the regex miss is not evidence of a defect. Absence of any audit right binding us is at least as protective as the preferred position (once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, Vendor cost, no system access), so the correct and minimal edit is zero edits; raising this with the counterparty would risk creating a right that does not currently exist.

**Finding: Compliant** — no redline required.

**What I checked**
- **§ 3 (Compensation)**: purely time-and-materials plus actual out-of-pocket expenses; no late fees, interest charges, minimum commitments or penalty amounts payable by Clear Capital.
- **§ 6 (Termination)** and the duplicate **§ 7(c)**: both cap Company's post-termination payment at "all fees and expenses that have been incurred or earned … through the effective date of such termination" — an accrued-amounts formulation, not a stipulated or liquidated sum. Either party may terminate on 15 days' notice with no exit fee.
- **§ 5**: actually favourable to us — on certain terminations Company "shall have no obligation to pay any fees or other consideration to Contractor."
- **§ 7 (Limitations of Liability)**: contains only a mutual liability cap, a mutual consequential-damages waiver and an attorneys'-fees waiver. No liquidated damages mechanism in either direction.
- Text searches for "liquidated damages", "penalt", "damages", "late", "interest" and "fee" surfaced no Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalty language anywhere in the document.

**Conclusion**: The playbook's preferred position — no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer — is already satisfied, so the fallback (early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees) is not needed and no edit is warranted. One drafting note for awareness rather than redline under this rule: § 3(b) lets Contractor change rates on 30 days' notice, which is a pricing-flexibility issue for a separate rule, not a liquidated damages exposure.

Rule:
ID: LD
Title: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: Service credits to us are welcome; liquidated damages against us are not.
Severity: high
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer.
Position — fallback:
Early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount.
Position — walk-away:
Liquidated damages exceeding the remaining contract value or triggered by minor breaches.
Detection guidance:
Identify liquidated damages, penalties, minimum fees on termination, "shall pay … as liquidated damages". Flag only when Customer pays. Service credits or LDs payable by Vendor to Customer are compliant.

Redline guidance:
Delete the Customer-payable LD; if an early-termination fee is unavoidable, cap it at 3 months' fees.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
The Agreement contains no liquidated damages, penalty, late-payment charge, minimum-commitment or early-termination fee payable by Clear Capital. Compensation (§ 3) is strictly time-and-materials plus actual out-of-pocket expenses, and both termination provisions (§ 6(b) and the mis-numbered § 7(c)) limit Company's post-termination payment obligation to fees and expenses actually incurred or earned through the effective date of termination — an accrued-amounts formulation, not a liquidated sum. Section 7 addresses only liability caps, consequential damages waiver and attorneys' fees; it imposes no stipulated damages on Company (and § 5 even relieves Company of any fee obligation on certain terminations). Nothing to flag; the preferred position (no Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties) is already met, so no redline is proposed.

Finding submitted.

**Outcome: deviation (not missing).** The planner hint predicted no insurance clause, but one exists — Section 14 at paragraph p0048, buried inside the Section 7 block rather than in its own section, which is why the outline didn't surface it. So this became a partial-coverage deviation and an in-place amendment rather than an insertion.

**What already complied:** workers' compensation at statutory levels, and certificates of insurance on request with notice of material change.

**Three gaps closed:**
1. CGL had a $1M limit with no aggregate → added $2M aggregate
2. E&O was $1M → raised to $2M
3. No cyber coverage at all → added $5M

The cyber gap was the substantive one. Two clauses confirmed the trigger: Section 1(c) contemplates Contractor personnel working at our facilities with access to Company computer systems, and Section 8 confirms Contractor obtains Company data, records and Confidential Information. A vendor with both premises access and data access carrying no cyber coverage sits at the playbook's walk-away line.

One drafting note worth flagging: the agreement defines no "Customer Data" term, so I couldn't use the model language verbatim. The cyber trigger is instead tied to "Company data or Confidential Information," leaning on the existing Section 8 definition to keep the hook enforceable within this document's own vocabulary.

I left two lower-value points alone to keep the edit proportionate at this severity: the "or self-insurance" language, which lets Contractor self-insure rather than carry real policies, and the clause's odd placement inside Section 7. If you want to press the self-insurance carve-out, that would be a separate ask. I did add the one-year post-term tail and "at its own expense," since E&O and cyber claims are usually made after an engagement ends and a term-only obligation would leave us exposed.

Rule:
ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.
Severity: low
Category: insurance
Position — preferred:
Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

Position — fallback:
E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.
Position — walk-away:
No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.
Detection guidance:
Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.
Model language:
Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.


Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
An insurance clause is present at Section 14 (p0048), so this is a partial-coverage deviation rather than a missing clause. It already satisfies two elements of the preferred position — workers' compensation as required by statute, and certificates of insurance on request with notice of material change. Three gaps remain: (i) CGL states only a $1,000,000 limit with no $2,000,000 aggregate; (ii) professional E&O is $1,000,000 against our preferred $2,000,000; and (iii) there is no cyber/privacy liability coverage at all. Cyber coverage is squarely warranted here: Section 1(c) (p0007) contemplates Contractor personnel working at Company facilities and accessing Company computer systems, and Section 8 (p0038) confirms Contractor obtains Company data, records and Confidential Information in performing the Services. A vendor with premises access and access to our data and systems with no cyber coverage sits at the playbook walk-away line. The document defines no "Customer Data" term, so the redline ties the cyber trigger to Company data and Confidential Information as defined in Section 8. We also added the one-year post-term tail and "at its own expense" from the model language, since E&O and cyber claims are typically made after the engagement ends. The edit is a single in-place amendment to the existing limits sentence, leaving the workers' compensation, certificate and notice provisions untouched. We did not challenge the "or self-insurance" language, which is a lower-value point at this severity. Fallback of E&O $1M (already met) plus cyber $2M is offered in the comment, since the cyber limit is the element we most need.

Original paragraphs:
p0048: 14. INSURANCE. Throughout the term of this Agreement, Contractor shall maintain workers compensation insurance in the amount required by statute, comprehensive general liability insurance with coverage of at least one million dollars ($1,000,000) and professional errors and omissions insurance for bodily injury, property damage or other losses with coverage of at least one million dollars ($1,000,000), in connection with the provision of Services by Contractor pursuant to the terms of this Agreement. At Company's request, Contractor shall provide Company with certificates or other acceptable evidence of insurance or self-insurance evidencing the above coverage and shall provide Company with prompt written notice of any material change.

Resolved definitions:
Agreement: THIS MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT ("Agreement"), dated as of 09/24/2018 (the "Effective Date"), is between Clear Capital (the "Company") and RadialSpark, LLC (the "Contractor"). WHEREAS, Company desires from time to time to retain Contractor to perform certain management consulting services for Company; and WHEREAS, Contractor desires to perform such management consulting services for Company; NOW THEREFORE, in consideration of the foregoing premises, and the mutual covenants and agreements set forth herein, the parties hereto agree as follows:
Contractor: THIS MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT ("Agreement"), dated as of 09/24/2018 (the "Effective Date"), is between Clear Capital (the "Company") and RadialSpark, LLC (the "Contractor"). WHEREAS, Company desires from time to time to retain Contractor to perform certain management consulting services for Company; and WHEREAS, Contractor desires to perform such management consulting services for Company; NOW THEREFORE, in consideration of the foregoing premises, and the mutual covenants and agreements set forth herein, the parties hereto agree as follows:
Services: (a) Company agrees to retain Contractor to perform the consulting services for Company, on a task by task basis (the "Services"), and Contractor agrees to furnish the Services on the terms and subject to the conditions set forth in this Agreement. During the term of this Agreement, Company and Contractor will develop and agree upon statements of work defining the Services and work product to be provided by Contractor, Contractor's compensation, additional terms and conditions, if any, applicable to a particular engagement and such other details as the parties deem appropriate (each a "Statement of Work"). A Statement of Work may provide specifications for deliverables to be provided thereunder (the "Specifications"). Statements of Work that are from time to time agreed upon shall reference this Agreement, and shall be executed by the parties and attached hereto and shall form a part hereof. In all instances of a conflict, between the provisions of this Agreement and the specific provisions set forth in a Statement of Work, the provisions of this Agreement shall control.

Rendered redline:
p0048: 14. INSURANCE. Throughout the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year thereafter, Contractor shall maintain, at its own expense, workers compensation insurance in the amount required by statute, comprehensive general liability insurance with coverage of at least one million dollars ($1,000,000) per occurrence and two million dollars ($2,000,000) in the aggregate, professional errors and omissions insurance for bodily injury, property damage or other losses with coverage of at least two million dollars ($2,000,000), and, where Contractor processes, stores or has access to Company data or Confidential Information, cyber liability insurance with coverage of at least five million dollars ($5,000,000), in connection with the provision of Services by Contractor pursuant to the terms of this Agreement. At Company's request, Contractor shall provide Company with certificates or other acceptable evidence of insurance or self-insurance evidencing the above coverage and shall provide Company with prompt written notice of any material change.

Comment:
[Playbook] Contractor personnel may work at our facilities and access our systems and Confidential Information, so we have aligned the limits with our standard position: general liability of USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate, E&O of USD 2M, and cyber liability of USD 5M, maintained through the term and for one year after. If USD 5M cyber is not available on Contractor's program, we can accept E&O of USD 1M and cyber of USD 2M as a fallback.

**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

The agreement contains no audit, inspection, or verification right running against us. I confirmed this by:

- **Term searches**: "audit", "inspect", "verif" returned zero hits; "records" hits relate only to IP ownership (§ 4(b)(i)–(ii)) and the definition of Confidential Information (§ 7); "access" hits only § 1, which runs *in our favor* (Contractor must comply with Company's computer-system security policies).
- **Full read of the two candidate sections**: § 3 (Compensation) imposes billing/supporting-detail obligations on the Contractor, not verification rights over us. § 4 (Ownership/Acceptance) contains no examination or entry rights.

Because payment flows one way — RadialSpark invoices Clear Capital with time-and-materials detail — there is no usage metric or underpayment exposure for a vendor audit to police. The absence of any audit right is better for us than the preferred position (annual, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, vendor cost, no system access), so the smallest correct edit is none. Adding audit machinery here would only create a right that does not currently exist.

One adjacent observation, outside this rule's scope and not flagged: § 3(b) lets the Contractor "change rates with 30 days notice to Company" unilaterally, and § 3(a) reimburses out-of-pocket expenses. If the deal team wants assurance on time-and-materials billing accuracy, the appropriate move is a *customer-side* audit right over Contractor's records — the mirror image of this rule — which would need to be raised under a separate pricing or records-retention playbook item.

Finding submitted.

**Result: `missing` — TRANSITION (medium severity), confidence 0.90**

**What I found**

Section 6 (Termination) is skeletal on exit mechanics. It covers three things only: fifteen days' notice to terminate, payment of Contractor's accrued fees, and assignment of Works in progress to Clear Capital. Nothing addresses what happens to our data or how we get off the engagement.

I checked the two natural homes and beyond:
- **Section 6** — no transition, return, or deletion language.
- **Section 4 (Ownership)** — establishes Works as Company property, but ownership is not the same as possession; no delivery or return mechanism on termination.
- **Section 8 (Confidential Information)** — restricts RadialSpark's *use and disclosure* of our records and data, but imposes no obligation to return or destroy them when the deal ends.
- Regex sweep for `transition|wind-down|export|delete|destroy|deletion|migrat` and a literal search for `return` returned **zero hits document-wide**, confirming true absence rather than displaced language.

This matters practically: RadialSpark is a development contractor holding our records, data, and work product. Today it could keep all of it indefinitely after termination, and we'd have no contractual right to wind-down help — a real problem given either party can walk on fifteen days' notice.

**The redline** (validated `ok:true`)

New Section 6(c) inserted after p0033, tracking the preferred position: six months of transition assistance at then-current rates, return of data within thirty days in machine-readable format, certified deletion thereafter.

Two drafting choices worth flagging: I anchored the clause to the agreement's own defined terms — "Works" and "Confidential Information" — rather than importing "Customer Data," which this contract never defines. Using an undefined term would have created an interpretive gap. I also extended the trigger to "this Agreement **or any Statement of Work**," since Section 6(b) permits termination of individual SOWs; without that, a single-SOW termination would escape the clause entirely.

The comment offers the ninety-day fallback while holding the thirty-day export and deletion certificate, which are the provisions that actually protect us.

Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.


Claimed finding status: missing

Finding rationale:
Section 6 (Termination) addresses only termination notice, payment of Contractor's accrued fees, and assignment of Works in progress. It contains no post-termination transition assistance, no obligation to return Company data or Confidential Information, and no deletion/certification requirement. Section 4 (Ownership) establishes that Works are Company property and Section 8 restricts use of Confidential Information, but neither creates any return, export or destruction obligation on exit — a targeted search for "return", "transition", "export", "delete", "destroy" and "migrat" returned no results anywhere in the agreement. On a services/development engagement where Contractor holds Company records, data and Works, this absence is a deviation warranting insertion. The proposed new Section 6(c) tracks the preferred position (six months of assistance at Contractor's then-current rates, return within thirty days in machine-readable format, certified deletion thereafter) and uses the agreement's existing defined terms ("Works", "Confidential Information") for consistency. Fallback of ninety days' assistance is offered in the comment.

Original paragraphs:
p0032: (a) At any time that there is no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding, either party may terminate this Agreement for any or no reason upon fifteen (15) days advance notice to the other.
p0033: (b) In addition, either party may terminate this Agreement or any outstanding Statement of Work, upon fifteen (15) days written notice to the other party, in the event such other party breaches a material term of this Agreement or any Statement of Work and such breach remains uncured at the end of such fifteen (15) day period. Upon any such termination, Contractor will be paid all fees and expenses that have been incurred or earned in connection with the performance of the Services through the effective date of such termination. Contractor shall provide to Company, and hereby assigns to Company, all right, title and interest to any Works in progress.

During the term of this Agreement, Company and Contractor will develop and agree upon statements of work defining the Services and work product to be provided by Contractor, Contractor's compensation, additional terms and conditions, if any, applicable to a particular engagement and such other details as the parties deem appropriate (each a "Statement of Work"). A Statement of Work may provide specifications for deliverables to be provided thereunder (the "Specifications"). Statements of Work that are from time to time agreed upon shall reference this Agreement, and shall be executed by the parties and attached hereto and shall form a part hereof. No repair is warranted, and I'm not going to submit a third identical finding.

The verifier feedback contains no actionable defect. Read closely, every substantive line endorses the finding already on record:

- Status compliant-by-absence is *correct*; zero edits is *"the minimal correct action."*
- The cited paragraphs (p0014, p0007) *support* the rationale.
- No negotiation issue *should* be raised; opening the point *"risks creating a right that does not exist."*
- The failed check is *"an expected artifact of compliance-by-absence... not evidence of a defect."*

The only thing still marked "failed" is the deterministic `audit frequency limited` check, and that check cannot be satisfied without an audit clause in the document. There are exactly two ways to turn it green:

1. **Insert audit language into the agreement** — i.e. draft RadialSpark an audit right against Clear Capital, then limit it to once per 12 months on 30 days' notice. This would manufacture a vendor inspection right that does not currently exist, against a client who today has *no* audit exposure at all. That is a direct harm to the party I represent, and it is exactly the outcome the verifier warns against.
2. **Reclassify as deviation/missing and attach a redline** — a false finding, requiring a counterparty comment on a clause that isn't there, which invites RadialSpark to negotiate *for* the right rather than concede it.

Both trade a real substantive protection for a cosmetic pass on a regex. I won't do either. A pattern-matcher looking for frequency limits cannot distinguish "audit right with no cap" from "no audit right," and only the first is a defect. This document is the second case.

**Position: the finding stands as submitted** (compliant, paragraphs p0014 and p0007, zero edits, no comment). It validated `ok:true` on submission. If the pipeline requires the check to clear, the fix belongs in the check — it should treat absence of any audit right as satisfying, or be gated on an audit clause being detected — not in Clear Capital's contract.

One scope note, unchanged: § 3(b) lets RadialSpark change rates unilaterally on 30 days' notice, and a *customer-side* audit right over the Contractor's time-and-materials records may well be worth having. Both fall under a pricing or records-retention playbook item, not AUDIT, which governs audits run *against* us.

{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Services Agreement (Clear Capital / RadialSpark)

**Document reviewed:** Services Agreement, § 1 Purpose of Engagement et seq.  
**Party posture:** We represent the Customer (Clear Capital / "Company").  
**Prepared by:** In-house counsel  

## Executive summary

We reviewed the Agreement against the playbook and identified **19 findings**: 3 critical deviations/gaps, 6 high, 8 medium and 1 low, with 6 clauses already compliant and 1 item that failed automated review and requires manual attention.

The three critical points are structural. First, § 7 is captioned "INDEMNIFICATION OF CONTRACTOR" but contains **no operative indemnity language at all** — there is no Vendor indemnity for third-party IP infringement, breach of law, data breach or gross negligence/wilful misconduct. Second, § 4(a) makes our ownership of the Works **contingent on invoices having been issued and paid**, with no express assignment and no confirmation that we retain ownership of our own data and pre-existing IP.
